chapter: Trent's band: touring, sidemen and breakup
title: A racist radio introduction and Crooke faces down a bully
summary: At WFAA opening night the announcer introduces them with a slur; the next day Crooke subdues a would-be tough with his revolver.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: We were broadcasting, and the announcer was the owner and opening night he said, ladies and gentlemen, I want you to hear the greatest nigger band you ever heard in your life, and we all turned around and looked, what is this; just give me one more minute to tell you about these niggers. These niggers are from Texas, they played the Adolphus Hotel--boy, he talked about us.

The next day we were playing for a colored dance, and they had an act--McKinney's Cotton Pickers played the night before and one of the boys got beat up by--and they were big guys--but they'd beat up a guy in those days for nothing, and get away with it. So we were standing out in front of the theatre waiting for the theatre to open, this colored theatre, and there were about seven of us and we took up a little of the sidewalk and this little guy came up on the side, just like a western bad man--what do

you boys mean by standing there--we didn't know what he was talking about, and we said we're waiting for the theatre to open. He said, you don't know who I am, you don't see nobody else on the street, do you; when I walk up the street everybody--all the niggers get off the street. So he stood there and took a long time for Crooke to walk up to him and grabbed him and picked him up--a little bit of a fellow--he said, you so and so, I'll break every bone--Crooke had his forty-five and the guy felt that--and when Crooke finally squeezed him and turned him loose, all he could see was cops running down the street. It was funny.
